name: Patrick Hilton

bio.statement: Hilton's voters' pamphlet statement lists his occupation as building operations manager.
Hilton's pamphlet statement lists a background as architectural designer, OPRD natural resource specialist and park ranger, Portland Parks, actor and artist.
bio.excerpt: Architectural Designer; Natural Resource Specialist & Park Ranger (OPRD); Portland Parks; Actor; Artist

bio.statement: Hilton's pamphlet statement lists study in planning, public policy and management at the University of Oregon and architecture at the University of Illinois Chicago.
bio.excerpt: Planning, Public Policy & Management, University of Oregon; Architecture, University of Illinois Chicago

positions.statement: Hilton's voters' pamphlet statement says he will champion adaptive reuse and historic preservation.
positions.excerpt: Champion adaptive reuse and historic preservation

positions.statement: Hilton's pamphlet statement proposes piloting community land trusts and co-housing to help renters become owners.
positions.excerpt: pilot community land trusts and co-housing that can turn renters like me into owners

positions.statement: Hilton's pamphlet statement says he would defend streets like Hawthorne and Belmont from generic corporate development.
positions.excerpt: Defend destination streets like Hawthorne and Belmont from generic corporate development

positions.statement: Hilton's pamphlet statement calls for expanding safe-sleeping infrastructure and safety ambassadors on corridors like Grand Avenue.
positions.excerpt: Expand safe-sleeping infrastructure and safety ambassadors on corridors like Grand Avenue

positions.statement: Hilton's pamphlet statement calls for protecting urban nature and taxing polluters and vacant units.
positions.excerpt: protect urban nature, tax polluters and vacant units

positions.statement: Hilton's pamphlet statement proposes redirecting consultant spending toward core services, the arts and community events.
positions.excerpt: redirect consultant spending toward core services, the arts, and events that keep neighbors connected

positions.statement: In a Portland Mercury candidate profile, Hilton says the Eastside Rezoning Project should be stopped, calling it lobbyist driven.

positions.statement: In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Hilton says the city should keep taxes as low as possible while maintaining core services.

collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 21 District 3 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF (with the full and large-print county pamphlets tried where the statement PDF was a scan; the pamphlet's candidate index marks candidates who filed no statement) plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form linked from portland.gov's 2026 city candidates page; (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the three articles that cover the whole District 3 field: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 3 council race' (2026-10-07), Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 3' (2026-09-09) and Portland Tribune 'Meet the Portland City Council District 3 candidates' (2026-10-13; Q&A — the Tribune says Sollitt, Pham, Parker, McCormick, Kelly and Frankenstein did not respond and Tucker withdrew). Multi-winner race: OPB states three council seats are available in District 3. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report.
